title: Hammock localization of a free factor is a pushout
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and mappingwise weak homotopy equivalences as in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. For a small category $A$ and wide subcategory $U$, let $H(A,U)$ be the reduced-hammock simplicial category: a $k$-simplex is a commutative rectangle with $k+1$ rows, fixed endpoints and identity endpoint vertical arrows, all downward vertical arrows in $U$, uniform horizontal direction in each column, and all leftward arrows in $U$. Adjacent column directions alternate and no column is all identities. Row deletion or repetition and concatenation are followed by reduction, deleting identity columns and composing adjacent equally directed columns; length zero is allowed precisely for equal endpoints. Let $O$ be a small set, let $D,W$ be free categories on $O$, and put $C=D*_O W$, the coproduct over the discrete category on $O$. Then there are canonical isomorphisms
$$H(C,W)\cong D*_O H(W,W),\qquad C[W^{-1}]\cong D*_O W[W^{-1}].$$
Here ordinary localization adjoins formal inverses subject to the composition and inverse relations, and ordinary categories are viewed as discrete simplicial categories. Under these isomorphisms the row-product comparison is $D*_O(H(W,W)\to W[W^{-1}])$. The pushout identifications are natural for functors preserving both specified factors.
